Schedule Accuracy

Scheduled sites ranked by how wrong their scheduled time looks

This ranks scheduled-pickup sites by how far the actual collection time sits from the scheduled time, and how one-directional that gap is. A site that is consistently early or consistently late by a wide margin is almost always a scheduling error — the scheduled time does not match when the run really happens — not a courier problem. Correcting those times lifts on-time performance without changing how routes are run. Click any row to see the individual pickups and their times.

Pickup siteScheduled pickupsMedian offset Early / on time / lateAssessmentSuggested correction
Early (>10 min before schedule) On time (within 10 min) Late (>10 min after schedule)

Route Efficiency

Scheduled routes ranked by how much their schedule needs adjusting

Every scheduled route is checked against when its stops are actually collected. A route flagged Adjust schedule has stops whose scheduled time is consistently wrong — click it to see each stop and the suggested new time. Recommendations are always per stop, never per route, because a single route often has some stops running early and others late; shifting the whole route would make half of them worse. Routes marked Operational have variable timing that reflects traffic, load or staffing, not a schedule that can be corrected.

Detailed Performance Summary — For Management Evaluations admin only

One summary per flagged driver: full metrics, a written performance summary, and recommended next steps. Written for a manager's use during a formal evaluation — not for reading aloud to the driver. Pattern-based observations only; these are not conclusions about cause, effort, or intent, and should be weighed alongside context the numbers can't capture.

Scan Validity Breakdown new rule

A piece earns scan credit only when e-Courier records it Completed and the action source is Scan. Manual completions by a dispatcher/coordinator no longer inflate the driver's scan percentage.
